name: Against My Better Judgement
tagline: Everyone hears the joke. Hardly anyone hears the hope.
epigraph: Bourbon, stirred dry. A four-line poem about San Francisco's 1906 fire ends on whiskey.
glassware: cocktail glass (about 180 ml), chilled, no ice
language_row: Wren's Resonance on reading v2: ready. Recognised, not flattered: an everyday scene (a letter "for your convenience", the groan, then the nod) with no side taken and no news named; the mask first, the hope underneath second. "This is me": "A joke is hard to laugh at; a hope is easy." Sceptic: "a sharp sense of humour" fits anyone; a hope protected *by* the joke doesn't. Fenced out: the Wise Fool's agreed story, the Subverter's "nodding along", the Scandalmonger's mocking the pious (y2 says faith isn't the target), *The Wink*'s hardship and mornings, the Morale Booster's cheering a room, *Still Yours*' eye-rolls. The drink acts out the person: dry and plain on top, the whiskey as the punchline, the pear in every sip and on no rim, tied in one clause to the hope Field sent out under another name. Pronoun warnings accepted: "his"/"him" in y3–y4 are Charles K. Field. ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/charles-k-field-hotaling-verse.md`. **No library page** (library.py finds no Hotaling, Field or *Cheerio*): Fred Minnick, "Hotaling Remembers 1906 Earthquake with Special Rye Release", fredminnick.com, 19 April 2024 (fetched 2026-09-30 for the family plan, the one version of the verse quoted); Online Archive of California, Stanford Special Collections M1533, Charles K. Field *Cheerio* records (fetched 2026-09-30); Wikipedia, "Charles K. Field" and "Hotaling Building" (tertiary, read 2026-10-04, used only to point to what it cites). Drink: *Cocktail Codex* (Manhattan family). Room notes: `work/jester-sage/`.
names_note: **Against My Better Judgement**, by a 2–1 vote (Wren, Hester); Tomás voted *Between the Lines*. It's the guest's own voice, hoping against the evidence (Hester), and makes no claim a page has to carry. Also considered: *Between the Lines* (Tomás: the hope never said, always there if you read closely; the pear in every sip, on no rim), *And Yet* (Hester's first pick), *The Small Print*, *Over Frisky* (from the verse; names the town more than the person), *Half Serious* (close to *Only Half Joking*).
open_items: **Web-only story, read once:** no library page carries Field, the verse or *Cheerio*. Minnick and the OAC record were read on 2026-09-30 for the family plan and weren't re-fetched (web budget); the card says so. SF Heritage and Holm 1962 are unread.

**One version of the verse** (Minnick's, V1); variants ("His churches", "spare") stay in the dossier. How it first circulated, and under whose name, isn't on any page: never "he signed it", never "famous at once".
**Every span counts from the fire, never the poem** (the poem's own date is on no page): "a hundred and more years after the fire", "two decades after the fire" (Hester's F1–F2, round 4).
**Bourbon is Tomás's choice**, not a claim about what the warehouse held (G4). No named bottle; Hotaling & Co. is a brand today.
**Kept out on purpose:** the quake's toll and images, any fire or smoke in the glass, *Cheerio*'s audience, "every morning", mocking faith.
